name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+21 partisan lean makes this one of the most Republican districts in the country
Incumbent Eric Burlison holds an overwhelming financial edge (~$960K on hand vs ~$34K for Hesketh)
Challenger Missi Hesketh's minimal fundraising (~$50K raised) signals a noncompetitive race
Prediction markets price a ~95% Republican hold; no polls or expert ratings contradict
model.rationale: The deep-red district, Burlison's incumbency, and a roughly 30-to-1 fundraising advantage leave no competitive signals, and markets price a near-certain Republican hold. The evidence points only to the size of the margin, not the outcome.
model.watch: A last-minute wave of outside spending against Burlison combined with a sharply favorable national environment for Democrats could narrow the margin, though not plausibly flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 7th District is among the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Eric Burlison is seeking re-election with a commanding financial edge, having raised about $1.5 million and holding roughly $960,000 on hand. Democratic challenger Missi Hesketh has raised only about $50,000, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and betting markets give Republicans roughly a 95 percent chance of holding the seat.

The forecast rests on district fundamentals. National conditions may be somewhat friendlier to Democrats than in recent cycles, but that is unlikely to overcome a structural disadvantage of more than twenty points combined with incumbency and a lopsided money gap. Burlison is a heavy favorite; the realistic question is his margin of victory, not the outcome.
